key_insight: A mixed unfitted finite element method computes photonic-crystal band structures on geometry-independent meshes while preserving the shifted de Rham structure to exclude spurious modes.
engineering_relevance: The approach avoids interface-fitted meshing and remeshing when inclusion shapes change, supporting photonic-crystal design studies.
method: Apply the Floquet–Bloch transform to the Maxwell eigenvalue problem.
Use a uniform background mesh and enforce periodicity by directly identifying degrees of freedom.
Construct compatible mixed finite element pairs with cut-position-independent inf-sup stability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports optimal eigenvalue and eigenspace convergence with mesh- and interface-position-independent constants, supported by extensive 2D and 3D numerical experiments.
watch_item: Implementation must preserve the shifted commuting structure and correctly handle cut interfaces; the abstract provides no runtime or scalability benchmarks.
paper_title: Mixed Unfitted finite element approximation of band structures in photonic crystals
